title: Interpretable Survival Machine Learning Framework
text: 1. Fit model 2. Predict survival probabilities predict() also returns quantities via type: "risk" (1 - S(t)), "chf", "hazard", "rmst", "quantile", "median". 3. Evaluate model performance score model data trained , pass newdata; score predictions made elsewhere, pass survival matrix outcome. 4. Compare multiple learners compare() evaluates every learner resampling folds, results paired; tune = TRUE tunes tunable learner first.  5. Bring learner custom learner list fit function predict function returns one row per subject one column per time. works every verb. 6. Visualize interpretation interpret() single entry point every explanation method, plot() draws result.

title: Decision-weighted scores for survival predictions — dwscore
text: object numeric matrix survival probabilities (rows = subjects, columns = times), example predict(). y survival::Surv() object one entry per row object. times Evaluation times. NULL reads "times" attribute column names form "t=<time>". weight Threshold weight: "range" uniform thresholds (default); decisions threshold range count. "survacc" spherical weight \((c^2 + (1 - c)^2)^{-3/2}\); loss 1 - SurvAcc. "brier" constant weight 2; loss Brier score. "log" weight \(1 / (c (1 - c))\); loss logarithmic score. "beta" Beta density parameters shape. thresholds Length-2 numeric range c(lower, upper) [0, 1] weight = "range" (default c(0.05, 0.20)). shape Length-2 numeric Beta parameters weight = "beta" (default c(2, 18), mean threshold 0.10).

title: Decision-weighted scores for survival predictions — dwscore
text: risk \(r = 1 - S(t \mid X)\) event status \(D = (T \le t)\), loss \(L_w(r, 0) = \int_0^r w(c)\, c\, dc\) subject event free t \(L_w(r, 1) = \int_r^1 w(c) (1 - c)\, dc\) subject event t. Right censoring handled inverse probability censoring weights Kaplan-Meier estimate censoring distribution: subjects event free t weighted \(1 / G(t)\), subjects observed event \(U \le t\) \(1 / G(U-)\), subjects censored t get weight zero. assumes censoring independent covariates. Range Beta weights integrate one, losses lie scale average regret per decision. evaluate(), compare() tune(), use metric ids "survacc" (SurvAcc, higher better) "range:<lower>-<upper>", example "range:0.05-0.20" (loss, lower better). need single time.

title: Decision-weighted scores for survival predictions — dwscore
code: m <- fit(Surv(time, status) ~ age + karno, veteran[1:100, ], "coxph") S <- predict(m, veteran[-(1:100), ], times = c(90, 180)) y <- Surv(veteran$time[-(1:100)], veteran$status[-(1:100)]) dwscore(S, y) #>   time          weight       loss #> 1   90 range(0.05,0.2) 0.03659910 #> 2  180 range(0.05,0.2) 0.01463964 dwscore(S, y, weight = "brier") #>   time weight       loss #> 1   90  brier 0.17687881 #> 2  180  brier 0.09568638 dwscore(S, y, weight = "range", thresholds = c(0.10, 0.30)) #>   time         weight       loss #> 1   90 range(0.1,0.3) 0.05470029 #> 2  180 range(0.1,0.3) 0.02342342  # the same scores inside the verbs (single time) S180 <- predict(m, veteran[-(1:100), ], times = 180) evaluate(S180, y = y, metrics = c("brier", "survacc", "range:0.05-0.20")) #> <survalis_eval> model = supplied predictions #>   scored once on 37 subjects (no resampling) #>   grid: 1 times in [180, 180] #>   brier           0.0960 #>   survacc         0.8980 #>   range:0.05-0.20 0.0150
